chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the believing man who marries the Jewish woman and the Christian woman, he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he attains a Muslim woman, so what does he do with the Jewish woman and the Christian woman?' So I said to him: 'If he happens to have passion for her?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he does, let him prevent her from drinking wine and eating the flesh of the swine, and know that there is a shortcoming upon him in his religion.'
ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim man do with his Jewish or Christian wife regarding their religious practices?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the practical application of marrying 'Ahl al-Kitab' by emphasizing the husband's duty to enforce dietary prohibitions (wine and pork) within the household, even if the wife retains her faith. The phrase 'ghadhatan fi dinih' (a slight imperfection in his religion) reflects the Shia scholarly view that while the marriage is valid, the persistence of her distinct religious identity and practices represents a minor spiritual deficiency for the Muslim husband, distinguishing it from the ideal of a fully integrated Muslim spouse.
